summary: Erik Braun is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his doctorate at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, also studying under Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun. He held posts at Harvard (attested 2010) and the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

Erik Erikson studied at the University of Oxford. His academic career included positions at Harvard University (circa 1934–1970), the University of California, Berkeley (circa 1939–1950), and the University of Pittsburgh (circa 1951–1960).

Erik Haarh was a Tibetologist and linguist who completed a doctorate at the University of Copenhagen. He worked as a librarian and department head at the Royal Danish Library (1956, 1962) before serving as a department head and professor at Aarhus University (1969, 1983).

Erik J. Hammerstrom specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010) and served as an assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).
Erik Pema Kunsang is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications (circa 1980) and as resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

Erik Zürcher was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, also studying under Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and Édouard Chavannes. He served as director at Leiden University (1961–1993).

Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian and linguist who completed his BA and PhD at Leiden University. He held academic posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), the International Institute of Social History (1990–1999, 2008–2012), and became a professor at Leiden University in 1997.

Erling von Mende is a sinologist who studied law and Sinology at Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne, where he completed his PhD (1969) and Habilitation (circa 1973–1979). He served as a professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin (1983–2007).
Ernest Arthur Gardner was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Gonville and Caius College (circa 1880–1884). He later held an academic appointment at the University of London (1924–1926).

Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig Harris, and Henry Hoenigswald. He taught at the University of Pennsylvania (1950–1989) and edited the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

Ernest Fenollosa was a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and history who studied at Harvard and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1878), Tokyo National Museum (1888), and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1890–1896).

Ernest John Henry Mackay was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Bristol. He served as Custodian of Antiquities for the Government of Mandatory Palestine (1919–1922) and Special Officer for Exploration for the Archaeological Survey of India (circa 1926–1932).

Ernest Renan was a scholar of religious studies, history, and linguistics who studied under Eugène Burnouf and Étienne Marc Quatremère. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and served as professor of Hebrew (1861) and administrator (1883) at the Collège de France.

Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He was a professor at Brown University from 1964 and Board of Governors Professor of Philosophy at Rutgers University (1998–2006).

Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Bonn and Göttingen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and Christian August Brandis. He was a professor at Göttingen (1855–1867) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1844, 1863, 1867), and directed the Altes Museum (circa 1872–1896).

Ernst Förstemann was a linguist and historian who studied at Berlin and Halle-Wittenberg under Karl Lachmann, Franz Bopp, and August Friedrich Pott. He served as librarian at the Fürst zu Stolberg-Wernigerodesche Bibliothek (1851) and head of the Dresden Royal Public Library (1865–1887).

Ernst Fürlinger is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He served as Studienleiter at St. Virgil Salzburg (1991–2001) and held multiple researcher and leadership roles at the University for Continuing Education Krems (from 2007).

Ernst Gombrich was an art historian who studied at the University of Vienna. He held positions at the Warburg Institute as a research assistant (1936) and director (1959–1976), and worked at the University of London (1956–1959).

Ernst Haas was an Indologist who studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He worked at the British Museum (1866) and became Professor of Sanskrit at University College London in 1875.

Ernst Haeckel studied at the Frederick William University Berlin (Humboldt University of Berlin) from circa 1854 to 1857. He later held an academic appointment at the University of Jena from circa 1861 to 1909.
